clue.text: Methodical hospital worker

blocks.note: first meaning: neat, systematic and well arranged
second meaning: an attendant doing non-medical jobs on a ward

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of a tidy nurse, but the two parts are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for systematic, tidy habits and also a noun for a hospital attendant who carries out routine tasks.

clue.text: Girl's predilection arouses repugnance

blocks.note: Di is a short girl's name, here with the possessive 's
a taste for something is a liking or predilection

explanation.surface: A young woman's peculiar fondness for something stirs disgust in others.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive in Girl's is not grammar here: its S becomes a letter of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is a strong dislike or aversion, close in meaning to repugnance.

clue.text: Became tricky to conceal measuring system

indicators.note: what is concealed sits inside the following words, waiting to be found among their letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Something got awkward to keep secret, apparently a system of measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: The metric system is the decimal scheme of units such as metres and kilograms used for measurement.

clue.text: Game to overtake?

blocks.note: first meaning: the children's game of vaulting over a crouching player's back
second meaning: to jump ahead of rivals and pass them

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that the verb sense is figurative: in the game players literally pass one another by jumping.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a playground game of jumping over backs, and the verb means to surge past competitors by skipping stages.

clue.text: Prohibition doesn't apply about a fruit

indicators.note: about suggests turning around, so the short form is read back to front

blocks.note: a ban is a prohibition
N/A is the form-filling abbreviation for not applicable
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rule forbidding something is waived where a piece of fruit is concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: N/A is written on forms beside questions that do not apply; reversed it gives AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana is a long curved tropical fruit with a yellow skin, so it is an example of fruit.

clue.text: Sack of vegetables in the sitting-room?

definitions.note: a description: something found in a sitting-room

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: a bag holding pulses
second meaning: a soft pellet-filled seat used as furniture

explanation.surface: Someone has left a sack of greengrocery lying in the lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is the literal sense of the compound word; the question mark flags the loose second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the word is a bag of pulses; in everyday use it is a floppy cushion seat filled with polystyrene beads.

clue.text: Is drawn by advertisement?

definitions.note: a description: the thing that is drawn by a car

blocks.note: first meaning: a wheeled vehicle towed behind a car
second meaning: a short preview promoting a forthcoming film

explanation.surface: Something gets sketched by someone in a commercial, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Drawn looks like sketching, but here it means pulled along, as a caravan is.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a towed vehicle hitched behind a car and also a preview clip that promotes a film.

clue.text: Scolds following change to rebates

indicators.note: a change made to a word alters it, so its letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone is told off after altering the refunds given to customers.
explanation.definitionFit: To berate someone is to rebuke or criticise them angrily, the same as to scold them.

clue.text: Inevitably, sly increase appears wrong

indicators.note: if something is wrong it is out of order, so the letters must be rearranged

blocks.note: the eleven letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A sneaky rise in prices is bound to be seen as improper.
explanation.definitionFit: Necessarily means as a matter of course, unavoidably, which is what inevitably also expresses.

clue.text: No end of torment disturbed adviser

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter of the word is dropped
something disturbed has been moved out of place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Unending anguish has unsettled a counsellor.
explanation.definitionFit: A mentor is a trusted counsellor or guide who gives advice to a less experienced person.

clue.text: Details of previous schemes took one in

indicators.note: took in means accepted inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: ex- means former or previous
plans are schemes
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Particulars of earlier projects absorbed a single person.
explanation.walkthrough: Details is a verb here, as in sets out fully, not the plural noun it looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something is to set it out clearly and in detail, as the verb details means.

clue.text: Expression of regret when one abandoned adopted name

indicators.note: what is abandoned is left behind, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
an alias is an assumed or adopted name

explanation.surface: Someone sighs sadly on giving up a false identity.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an interjection uttered to show sorrow or disappointment about something that happened.

clue.text: Tidies up and vanishes

blocks.note: first meaning: removes things, as plates after a meal
second meaning: disperses, as fog or mist does

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like one person's actions, but the two halves are separate senses of the same phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means removing dishes or clutter, and also dispersing completely as fog lifts and disappears.

clue.text: Undo clothing in car?

definitions.note: a description: something found in a car

blocks.note: to reverse a decision is to undo it
gear is informal for clothes

explanation.surface: Someone unbuttons their outfit while sitting in a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Undo clothing suggests undressing, but each word is a separate piece; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverse gear is the gearbox setting in a car that makes it drive backwards.

clue.text: Extracts from changed scenes involving two points

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so extra letters are included among the others
changed means altered, so the combined letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
two compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: Clips taken from reworked film scenes include a couple of key moments.
explanation.walkthrough: Points in crosswords are often compass points: N, E, S or W.
explanation.definitionFit: An essence is a concentrated extract of a plant or flavouring, such as vanilla essence.

clue.text: Display affected behaviour making such entrances

blocks.note: arch means knowingly playful or affected
someone's ways are their habits or behaviour

explanation.surface: Showing off pretentious manners as one sweeps through the doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Archways are curved openings forming passages or entrances, so they are one kind of entrance.

clue.text: Retires from crime after giddy spell

indicators.note: after places the first named piece behind the second in the answer

blocks.note: a turn is a brief bout of dizziness
a sin is a wrongdoing or crime

explanation.surface: A criminal gives up a life of crime after a dizzy fit.
explanation.walkthrough: Retires means goes to bed here, not leaves work or crime.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn in is an informal idiom for going to bed, just as retiring for the night does.

clue.text: Following drink, fix up eating place

indicators.note: following puts the next piece behind the drink in the answer
in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: tea is a drink
to moor a boat is to fix it in place

explanation.surface: After a cuppa, someone arranges a café to visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea room is a small café serving tea, cakes and light meals, a modest eating establishment.

clue.text: Away from classes, as slightly unwell

blocks.note: out of means away from
sorts are kinds or classes

explanation.surface: A pupil is off school because they are feeling a bit poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of sorts is an idiom for feeling a little ill or below par.

clue.text: No 1 batsman is also useful in kitchen

blocks.note: first meaning: a cricketer who bats first in the innings
second meaning: a tool for prising lids off tins or bottles

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the two batsmen who start an innings are its openers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a cricketer who starts the batting and a device such as a tin opener for cans and bottles.

clue.text: Saunter along way to Tube

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a roll of paper or cloth is a cylinder, a tube

explanation.surface: Someone ambles down the road to the London Underground station.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's underground railway, but here it is just a cylinder shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is a leisurely walk, the same unhurried pace as a saunter.

clue.text: Bite into a sweet

blocks.note: first meaning: to grind with the teeth
second meaning: a soft chewy candy

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one action on a candy; a chew is also British for a soft toffee-like sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means working food with the teeth, and the noun names a soft chewy confection sold as candy.

clue.text: Confine Alastair in-house

blocks.note: to intern someone is to confine them, especially in wartime
Al is a short form of Alastair

explanation.surface: A man called Alastair is kept locked inside his home.
explanation.definitionFit: Internal means happening within an organisation, which is what in-house describes.

clue.text: Overturned drawer to discover prize

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, so the word is read back to front

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tips out a chest drawer and finds a trophy hidden inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is something given in recognition of merit or achievement, much like a prize.

clue.text: Tell them to go to blazes!

definitions.text: Tell them to go to blazes!

blocks.note: surface reading: an angry curse telling people to go to hell

blocks.clueFragment: Tell them to go to blazes!
blocks.note: setter's reading: people who are literally sent out to put out fires

explanation.walkthrough: Go to blazes is an insult, but taken literally it is the job of a fire crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire crew is dispatched to burning buildings, so they are the people sent to blazes.

clue.text: Showman's a pleasure seeker

blocks.note: a play is a theatrical show
a boy is a male, loosely a man

explanation.surface: An entertainer turns out to be a hedonist.
explanation.walkthrough: Showman must be read as two words, show and man, and the 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A playboy is a wealthy man who devotes himself to enjoyment and indulgence rather than work.
